items.title: triage-area aborts the classification pass on missing area:sparq-wrapper-gen label

labels.name: status:untriaged
labels.description: Triage LLM unavailable — cron will re-triage

labels.name: self-improvement
labels.description: Agent-discovered out-of-scope work for the self-improvement triage lane

items.body:
> 🤖 **SPARQ agent** — I am @jeswr's agent for the sparq-org/sparq RDF/SPARQL engine. @jeswr runs multiple agents; this was written by the SPARQ agent, not the PSS agent (prod-solid-server).

The scheduled area classifier aborts its entire classification pass when its generated plan includes `area:sparq-wrapper-gen`, which is absent from the repository's labels. This prevents otherwise valid rows from reaching the write loop.

Evidence: [run 34299934012, job 102304479961](https://github.com/sparq-org/sparq/actions/runs/34299934012/job/102304479961), on main `a42a9e89dec485f6a319c47cb3635c59cb5a2270`, attempt 1. The internal fixtures and independent tests passed; the live classification step then exited 2 with `ERROR: rule table produced labels that do not exist: ['area:sparq-wrapper-gen']`. The [unknown-label guard](https://github.com/sparq-org/sparq/blob/a42a9e89dec485f6a319c47cb3635c59cb5a2270/scripts/triage-area.py#L738-L746) returns before the classification/write loop, so this occurrence performed no classification or unpark writes.

A direct label lookup returned 404, and a fresh GraphQL lookup on 2026-09-09 returned null while main remained at the same commit. Exact-label and broader triage-area searches found no matching issue. Related #6335 concerns truncating enumeration at 500 labels; it does not explain this currently absent label and should remain a separate repair. The failed run does not identify the originating issue row, so the precise classification path and intended supported owner area still need to be established.

The focused repair should identify that path, use the appropriate existing supported area mapping if one is justified, and add a regression fixture for the actual input. Preserve the unknown-label fail-closed guard and prove an unsupported label still causes zero writes. Improve the diagnostic to identify the offending row/path if needed. Do not automatically create labels, guess a broad routing replacement, or replay live work as part of diagnosis.

Discovered during bounded operational triage alongside #4246; no routing change has been made.

items.title: Seed line-% coverage floors for the 26 crates in coverage-gate.py AWAITING_SEED

labels.name: status:untriaged
labels.description: Triage LLM unavailable — cron will re-triage

labels.name: self-improvement
labels.description: Agent-discovered out-of-scope work for the self-improvement triage lane

items.body:
Follow-up to #6121. That issue's drift-PREVENTION half is done: `scripts/coverage-gate.py --check-untracked` (wired into the no-compile `coverage-floors` job) now fails if a crate under `crates/` has neither a floor row in `bench/coverage-floor.json` nor a declaration, and the 26 un-floored crates are enumerated in `AWAITING_SEED` instead of being silently invisible.

What is still OPEN is the half that cannot be done in a no-compile change: those 26 crates still carry NO line-% floor, so the ratchet gates nothing for them. Seeding each one needs, per crate:

1. a `PER_COMMIT_CRATES` entry plus a `SHARD_GROUPS` slot in `scripts/coverage.sh` (without the slot, `coverage.sh --check-shards` reds), rebalancing the LPT bin-packing so no shard's wall-clock regresses;
2. for the 15 crates tagged `_SEED_NEEDS_FEATURES`, a `measure()` `case` arm naming the measured feature set (their opt-in features are default-off, so a default build reports a non-representative number);
3. an actual `cargo llvm-cov` run on a quiet box, then `coverage-gate.py --seed`.

Each seeded crate must have its `AWAITING_SEED` row deleted in the same PR — `--check-untracked` fails on a stale declaration, which is what keeps that list shrink-only.

The 3 crates tagged `_SEED_EMPTY_SEAM` (`sparq-wrapper-gen`, `sparq-wrapper-integration`, `sparq-wrapper-shacl`) are doc-only `src/lib.rs` stubs today; they only need a floor once the seams are implemented.

Best done as several PRs (one shard group at a time) rather than one, so a rebalance regression is attributable.

items.title: bench/coverage-presence.json is missing 25 crates, including sparq-lws-wasm

labels.name: self-improvement
labels.description: Agent-discovered out-of-scope work for the self-improvement triage lane

items.body:
Found while wiring sq-gg0qq.11 (#2741).

`scripts/coverage-presence.py --seed` scans every directory under `crates/` that has a `Cargo.toml`, but `bench/coverage-presence.json` has not been re-seeded since several crates were added, so 25 of the 67 crates carry no test-presence floor at all: sparq-acbench, sparq-arrow, sparq-conformance-floors, sparq-crdt, sparq-difftest, sparq-e2ee-ng, sparq-fedplan-mpc, sparq-http3, sparq-jsonld-registry, sparq-kb, sparq-lws-wasm, sparq-mcp, sparq-metamorph, sparq-reason-diff, sparq-reason-dl, sparq-shaclc, sparq-terse, sparq-trust, sparq-vc, sparq-wac-oracle, sparq-wrapper, sparq-wrapper-gen, sparq-wrapper-integration, sparq-wrapper-shacl (plus sparq-jsonld, which is in the floor file but not the presence file).

Each of those crates could lose every one of its tests without the presence gate noticing — which is precisely the failure mode the gate was built for (its header: 'delete every test in a crate and its line% just drops a little'). `sparq-lws-wasm` (26 counted `#[test]`s, the wasm Solid-pod profile of the LWS estate) is the one adjacent to #2741's scope; the rest are a general sweep.

#2741 deliberately did not run a blanket `--seed`: that rewrites floors for all 42 tracked crates in one commit and is not reviewable inside a server-crate CI bead. The follow-up should run `python3 scripts/coverage-presence.py --seed`, review the per-crate deltas, and land the new floors with notes.
